c.tagline: Okayama's canal town of white-walled warehouses, Western art, and artisan denim.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered and reliable; ride-hailing (GO, DiDi) only dispatches licensed metered taxis rather than private cars, so hailing at a rank or the station is often simplest.

emergency.note: 110 reaches the police and 119 reaches fire and ambulance; English support is limited, so the Japan Visitor Hotline (050-3816-2787) offers 24/7 multilingual help.

hood_desc: The lovingly preserved Edo-era merchant quarter of white-walled, black-tiled kura warehouses along a willow-lined, koi-filled canal, home to the Ohara Museum of Art; the must-see heart of any visit.

The modern hub around Kurashiki Station and the Achi shopping district, with department stores, the Ario mall, and the bulk of the city's hotels; a convenient, walkable base 10-15 minutes from the Bikan quarter.
The atmospheric old streets just east of the Bikan canal, where renovated machiya townhouses now hold indie cafes, craft shops, and small galleries; suits travelers after a quieter, creative pocket.

A southern seaside district and the birthplace of Japanese jeans, whose Kojima Jeans Street is lined with denim ateliers and boutiques; a shopping-focused day out about 20 minutes by train from the center.
A historic former port town on the west side of the city, with temples, old streets, and a low-key local feel well off the tourist trail; quiet and residential.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout Japan.

transit.hours: JR trains run from around 5:00 AM to midnight; local city buses run from early morning to about 9:00-10:00 PM, so evenings often fall to taxis.
transit.note: Kurashiki has no metro or tram — JR West trains (San'yo Main Line, plus the San'yo Shinkansen at neighboring Shin-Kurashiki) handle regional travel, while local buses and taxis cover the city; the Bikan Historical Quarter is a flat 10-15 minute walk from Kurashiki Station.
transit.pay: Tap a nationwide IC card (ICOCA, Suica, etc.) or a contactless card on JR trains and most buses; cash is accepted onboard buses. A local JR hop is around ¥200 (~US$1.40).

bus: Highway buses to Osaka, Kobe & Hiroshima

transit.m: Airport Limousine Bus direct to Kurashiki Station (~45 min, ¥1150)
Airport Limousine Bus to Okayama Station, then JR San'yo Line to Kurashiki (~15 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary in Japan and can cause confusion; excellent service is standard and already included.
